html:
The Miwa are an Aboriginal people of the north Kimberley in Western Australia, in country inland from the coast near the King Edward River.

Their speech is usually counted as a dialect of Wunambal, one of the Worrorran languages. Neighbours on the map are the Gaambera, the Kwini and the Wunambal. The region is known for its rock art, including Wandjina paintings. Little else is recorded about the Miwa as a separate group. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Miwa are an Aboriginal people of the north Kimberley in Western Australia, in country inland from the coast near the King Edward River.
